newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel slow in giving Palestinians entry permits.
newsitem.headline: Israel slow in giving Palestinians entry permits.

text.p: Palestinian officials said on Tuesday that despite Israel's announcement it would further ease a closure imposed on the West Bank and Gaza Strip, additional entry permits had yet to be received from Israel.
They also said some Palestinians who already had permits were being turned back by Israel for no apparent reason.

"We were informed by Israeli authorities of an easing of the closure, but...none of the Palestinian workers benefited from the new measures today," Said Mudallal, a Palestinian Labour Ministry official, told Reuters.
The Israeli army said on Monday it would permit more Palestinians to work in Israel, easing the closure imposed last month after a Moslem militant bombed a Tel Aviv cafe.

PLO officials said about 10,000 Palestinian workers entered the Jewish state on Sunday when Israel first eased the closure imposed after the March 21 blast which killed the bomber and three Israeli women.
Nasser Sarraj, director of the Palestinian Trade and Industry Ministry, said dozens of Palestinians who already have entry permits have recently been turned back at the border without any reason.
"Furthermore... Israel has given permits to 1,750 businessmen to enter Israel but is allowing only 700," he added.
Before the March closure, 50,000 Palestinians worked in Israel. Palestinians condemn closures as collective punishment.

Mudallal said the army told the Palestinian Authority it had raised the minimum age for a work permit from 30 to over 35, which would allow another 10,000 workers to enter Israel. The workers have to be married.
Israel believes the marriage requirement and age limit cut the risk of suicide bombers entering its territory.
